title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The image is extremely faint. Its text matches what is given as the NEXT page's transcription almost word for word. This page is probably a faint copy, show-through or duplicate of that cleaner sheet, so I read it through that transcription.

Setting (Grothendieck's Teichmüller-tower programme). G is a stable graph, the dual graph of a stable marked curve.
- A = set of edges (nodes); \vec A = set of oriented edges or half-edges, two per edge.
- G^b = the graph cut open at all edges, i.e. the normalization: each half-edge becomes a new marked point.
- \hat M_G = the moduli of curves of type G with its branches separated (normalization of the boundary stratum).
- SP_G = the principal G_m^A-bundle on \hat M_G whose fibre over a curve is the product over the nodes of the lines T_p ⊗ T_q (smoothing parameters). Equivalently, the punctured normal bundle of the stratum in \bar M_{g,ν}. The P_{G,C} are its quotients by subtori.

Claim 1. SP_G is induced from a finer bundle SP_{G^b}: the G_m^{\vec A}-torsor of nonzero tangent vectors at all branch points, a product of punctured ψ-line bundles. The induction is along the multiplication map G_m^{\vec A} → G_m^A, (t_p, t_q) ↦ t_p t_q. This is the formula N_{node} = T_p ⊗ T_q. Grothendieck notes this map is 'libre' over \hat M_G.

Claim 2 (topological/discrete shadow). ST_G, the extension of the Teichmüller groupoid T_G by Z^A, is the groupoid analogue of the punctured tubular neighbourhood of the stratum. The Z^A are the Dehn twists around the vanishing cycles. ST_G is induced from ST_{G^b}, an extension by Z^{\vec A} (twists around the new punctures), along the sum map Z^{\vec A} → Z^A.

NB 1. Since T_G is an extension of RT_G by Z^A, it is determined by its pushouts T_{G,a}: the extensions by Z, one for each edge a. It even suffices to know the T_{G,\bar a} = T_{G^b,\bar a}, one for each half-edge \bar a.

NB 2 (margin). T_{⊔ G_α} ≅ ∏ T_{G_α}.

Conclusion. Everything reduces to constructing ST_{g,I} ≅ T^!_{g,ν}, the Teichmüller groupoid of curves with nonzero tangent vectors at the marked points. This is an extension of T_{g,I} by Z^I. Equivalently, one needs the I extensions S(T_{g,I})_i by Z, one per marked point (the twist around puncture i, i.e. the boundary-circle central extension). Likewise, the construction of the tori S'T_G → ST_G for generalisations G' of G is to be reduced to elementary generalisations. That last point is left 'à voir en concret'.

Purpose. This builds the 'gluing data' of the Teichmüller tower: how the groupoids of lower strata sit, via tubular neighbourhoods, inside those of higher strata, reduced to the basic objects T_{g,ν} and their tangential (framed) versions.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The statement that SP_G comes from SP_{G^b} via G_m^{\vec A} → G_m^A is the standard identity N = T_p ⊗ T_q for the normal line at a node. It is correct, provided \hat M_G is the normalized stratum, not the stratum modulo Aut(G).

missed.claim: Grothendieck plans to reduce the construction of the 'tores' S'T_G → ST_G, attached to generalisations G' of the stable graph G (inclusions of tubular neighbourhoods between strata), to elementary generalisations. He leaves this 'à voir en concret'. It is a systematic functoriality of the tubular-neighbourhood extensions along specialisation of stable graphs; later literature does this only piecemeal (Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura).
missed.quote: la construction des tores S'T_G → ST_G, se réduit au [?] généralisations G' = G^♮ (C'est encore à voir en concret
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A coherent functorial system of this kind is what an operadic/modular-operad description of the profinite Teichmüller tower needs, and it bears on GT-actions. Existing treatments are close, though, so novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is the standard structure of normal bundles and Dehn-twist extensions at boundary strata. It is written cleanly in Grothendieck's own groupoid language, but specialists later developed it (Ihara–Nakamura, HLS). The only open item is the sketched functoriality along generalisations of graphs.
